Happy prediction Friday, Hawkeye fans! Tomorrow is the day you've all been waiting for for some time - a colossal matchup at Kinnick Stadium between No. 14 Iowa and No. 5 Ohio State on Saturday (2:30 p.m. CT, CBS). After careful consideration, here's how I see this battle playing out. Where/When To Watch Matchup: No. 5 Ohio State (3-1, 1-0) @ No. 14 Iowa (4-0, 1-0) Scheduled game time: Oct. 3 at 2:30 p.m. CT Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Weather: 68 degrees Announcers: Brad Nessler (play-by-play), Charles Davis (analyst), Jenny Dell (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Cole Krueger) Before we talk about the actual football game, let's begin this pick by talking about the electric atmosphere we're about to witness inside Kinnick Stadium on Saturday. This is easily Iowa's biggest home game at least in five years (No. 3 Iowa vs. No. 4 Penn State in 2021), and you probably have to go all the way back to the 2006 showdown between the Hawkeyes and Buckeyes to find a more important game in Iowa City. Iowa fans have waited for this game since the schedule came out in February, and the buzz in this city is palpable right now. College GameDay returning for the first time in 20 years has only increased it. The crowd might be the only advantage Iowa has on the gridiron, though. Though it blew a 20-point fourth quarter lead at Texas a few weeks ago, Ohio State still might be the most-talented team in the nation. The Hawkeyes are going to have their hands full against the Buckeyes, but the one thing Iowa will always have? Heart. That competitive grit was evident in the thrilling comeback victory over Michigan last weekend, and the Hawkeyes will certainly need it to keep pace with an explosive Buckeye offense. Speaking of offense, how will Iowa stop Jeremiah Smith? Smith is not only the best wide receiver in the country, he may just be the best player in the entire sport. Not only is he fast and an excellent route runner, his 6-foot-4, 222-pound frame makes him a dangerous threat in 50/50, red zone situations. Smith is likely going to make a few big plays in this game, but what concerns me the most is Iowa trying to get pressure on Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin. The Hawkeyes are never going to be a blitz-first team under Phil Parker, but have you seen how accurate Sayin is? He's not much of a running threat, but Iowa has to get pressure on him if it wants to stay in this ballgame. I think the Hawkeyes will get to Sayin a few times, but I don't think it's going to be enough. Iowa is going to cover the spread and move the ball against a shaky Ohio State defensive front , but the Buckeyes just make a few more big plays to pull away for a victory. picks.headline: David Pollack Picks Winner of Florida-Missouri
picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Florida-Missouri Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS A week ago, Florida was the team in prime position to deliver an upset while playing at home against an opponent, Ole Miss, that was coming off a huge win the previous week. The role is reversed in Week 5 for the No. 8-ranked Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC), who delivered their statement with a 52-28 win over that then-top-5 Rebels team and now must avoid a letdown of their own on the road against No. 25 Missouri (3-1, 0-1). Florida is set as a 5.5-point road favorite, per DraftKings Sportsbook , in a matchup that kicks off at 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday on ABC. College football analyst David Pollack dissected the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast. Alabama-Mississippi State, Ohio State-Iowa, Florida-Missouri AND MORE Week 5 CFB Picks https://t.co/8vWS9mTHpm "I want to be Missouri so bad in this matchup because everybody, everybody is like 'Oh, this Buster Faulkner guy's good. This Jon Sumrall guy's good!'" Pollack said of Florida's much ballyhooed new offensive coordinator and head coach. "We've been talking about it for a while -- welcome aboard everybody. "Here's the thing why this matchup becomes really awesome. You have that going for you, again, just like [with Florida vs. Ole Miss] last week, Missouri is playing at home. Florida is not sneaking up on anybody, right?" David Pollack Makes His Prediction For Florida-Missouri Pollack explained why he believes Missouri can potentially be a tough matchup for the Gators and what the Tigers are going to need to do to pull the upset. To put it simply, that requires slowing down running backs Jadan Baugh (600 rushing yards and 11 TDs on 7.2 yards per carry) and Duke Clark (259 yards and 3 TDs on 8.1 YPC) and a Florida rushing attack that ranks 11th nationally at 260.0 YPG while forcing quarterback Aaron Philo to make more plays with his arm. Philo, the Georgia Tech transfer who followed Faulker to Florida and is in his first season as a starter, has only attempted 87 passes in four games for 917 yards, 7 TDs and 2 INTs. Philo was 16-of-23 passing for 196 yards, 1 TD and 0 INTs plus a rushing TD in the win over Ole Miss. "Missouri's defense, watching them vs. Mississippi State, Missouri's defense always finds a way to be physical, they always find a way to be good in the front 7. They can rush the passer, 10 coming off the edge is consistently a problem," Pollack said of edge rusher Daeden Hopkins, who has 6 sacks and 2 forced fumbles already. "... Here's what I'm interested to see, this is the only thing that matters to me, can you put it in Philo's hands? Like literally, at some point who can make Philo be a QB because right now -- and I'm not knocking Philo, they're doing what they need to do and they're undefeated -- but right now Philo is getting worn out by handing that thing off. "Over 300 [rushing yards] a game the last two games against Auburn and Ole Miss. That is a feat, that is impressive. The offensive line is impressive. The system is impressive. Who is going to be the first to say, 'Philo, you've got to beat me'? And can he go through progressions and make those plays when it's not the easy stuff. Can you take away the layups, get him off schedule a little bit? If Missouri can do that at home, that will be interesting for me to watch. That's what I'm looking for the most in this game." Missouri lost its SEC opener 31-24 at Mississippi State last week and has played only one other Power 4 teams so far (a 38-21 win at Kansas). The Tigers are led by quarterback Austin Simmons, the Ole Miss transfer who has passed for 947 yards, 11 TDs and 0 INTs so far. Jamal Roberts (395 rushing yards and 3 TDs on 4.4 YPC) leads the rushing attack, that is still waiting for star Ahmad Hardy to return as he continues to recover and work back from an offseason gunshot wound. Ultimately, Pollack is picking the Gators to win by a comfortable margin. He's a believer in what Sumrall has built in his first season at Florida. "I trust Florida by this point now, I do. I trust them," Pollack said. "I will say this, Florida's receiving corps is banged up to heck. It's going to be very interesting to watch them. I've got Florida 38, Missouri 27ish. I'm trusting Florida on the road after a big game." Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. The program is off to its best start since 2019, but there is potential for an upset on Saturday . Ahead of the SEC showdown inside Memorial Stadium, CBS Sports writers Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer offer their predictions and picks for one of Week 5's best offerings. Both agree that Jon Sumrall and Co. will prevail, but they also concur that it will be a close one, taking the under on the 4.5-point spread. "Here's the Week 5 line that provided immediate pause when putting this week's card together — something ain't right here," Crawford begins. "Florida just rushed for 302 yards against Ole Miss and looks the part under first-year coach Jon Sumrall, while the Tigers are licking their road-woe wounds following a loss at Mississippi State. Winning away from home in the SEC is hard, and the Gators are going to get all they can handle according to oddsmakers." Crawford picks Florida to emerge triumphant from the gridiron grind, 31-27. Hummer, on the other hand, sees this finishing by a razor-thin margin. "This is probably the toughest test for Florida's offense so far this year," he notes. "The Tigers rank 19th nationally in yards allowed per carry and can at least limit Jadan Baugh. They also have a pass rush that can speed up Aaron Philo in obvious pass situations. Missouri does really miss Ahmad Hardy, ranking just 89th nationally in rushing yards per carry. But Austin Simmons has been excellent since transferring in from Ole Miss. Florida is a justified road favorite. But I think Missouri keeps this close enough to cover at home." Hummer predicts a narrow one-point victory, with a final score of 35-34 . away.headline: Mizzou injury status for Ahmad Hardy, 2 starting DEs vs Florida on official SEC report
away.blurb: As expected, Mizzou (3-1, 0-1 SEC) will again be without star running back Ahmad Hardy , who opened the week on the Wednesday, Sept. 30, report as "out." The Tigers also listed starting defensive ends Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen as "questionable" for the game against the Gators , which Eli Drinkwitz indicated would be the case during his press conference Tuesday. A questionable designation means neither Smith nor Kitchen have officially been ruled out but will continue to be assessed throughout the week. If Smith can't play, Daeden Hopkins and Jaden Jones are Mizzou's likely starters at defensive end. Smith was helped off of the field during MU's win over Troy this past Saturday. He attempted to return after being evaluated for a lower-body injury in the second half but only lasted one snap before returning to the sideline. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of MU's Week 4 game against Mississippi State and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. Hardy's timeline for a return after being shot in the upper leg in May is still uncertain. Florida (4-0, 2-0) listed two wide receivers — Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton — on the report as questionable. Both players have been involved in the Gators' wideout rotation this year, and Brown leads the team in receiving. For the second straight week, Mizzou also ruled out right tackle Josh Atkins, reserve safety JaDon Blair and backup tight end Gavin Hoffman for this weekend's game. The Tigers added backup linebacker Bobby Washington as "questionable" to face Florida. DE Langden Kitchen (Questionable) LB Bobby Washington (Questionable) WR Vernell Brown III (Questionable) WR Bailey Stockton (Questionable) The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. Gators defense forces quick three-and-out — Florida 45, Ole Miss 28 (Q4 | 8:42) Ole Miss goes three-and-out without gaining a yard, burning just 29 seconds before punting it back to Florida with 8:42 remaining. Florida doesn't give Ole Miss much time to enjoy making it a three-point game. After London Montgomery's 74-yard kickoff return puts the Gators at the Ole Miss 26, Aaron Philo immediately finds Amir Jackson for 23 yards down to the 3. The Gators get an immediate spark on the ensuing kickoff, though, as London Montgomery breaks a 74-yard return to the Ole Miss 26. Florida plays conservatively after getting the ball back with 1:11 remaining. Jadan Baugh runs twice before Aaron Philo finds Dallas Wilson for four yards on third-and-11, bringing out the punt team. Alec Clark flips the field with a 70-yard punt that goes out of bounds at the Ole Miss 2. The Rebels pick up 29 yards on three plays but run out of time. Clark has only had three chances to impress as Florida's punter. This should put him on the map... somewhere. Florida keeps the Rebels out of the end zone from there. DJ Coleman violently breaks up a pass intended for Samari Reed on second down, and Chambliss can't connect with Horatio Fields on third-and-4. Florida starts buried at its own 13 after an ill-advised kickoff return but spends the next 7:15 methodically marching 87 yards on 15 plays. Jadan Baugh gets things moving with gains of seven and two before Aaron Philo converts third-and-1 with his legs. Baugh takes it from there. He gains three yards on a direct snap and punches it in from two yards out on the next play for his second touchdown of the game. The Gators lead by two touchdowns three minutes before the break. The Gators' defense figures it out after that, though. Frazier loses two yards, Jayden Woods drops Caleb Odom for a 5-yard loss and Florida keeps a third-and-17 completion to six yards. Lucas Carneiro connects from 36 yards out, cutting Florida's lead to 10-3 with 10:13 remaining in the half. Penalties wipe out Gators touchdown as drive unravels — Florida 10, Ole Miss 0 (Q2 | 12:34) Baugh takes over from there, gains two yards, then punches it in from four yards out for the touchdown. Jadan Baugh wasted little time getting Florida’s offense moving, ripping off a 12-yard run on the Gators’ first play from scrimmage. Aaron Philo followed with a quick out route to Luke Harpring for another first down, to move Florida into Ole Miss territory. Florida passed its first major test last weekend against Auburn, and while Jon Sumrall and Co. out-duked the Tigers, it was far from a perfect performance — particularly the penalty issue that has once again reared its head. The offense overall still looks potent and the defense, despite a few letdowns, appears to be rounding into form. Jadan Baugh led the way with 142 yards and three touchdowns

home.headline: Two injured Missouri football defensive ends questionable for Florida game
home.blurb: Two injured Missouri football defensive ends questionable for Florida game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Two injured Missouri football defensive ends questionable for Florida game Mizzou coach Eli Drinkwitz said Tuesday, Sept. 29 that injured edge rushers Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen are both questionable for the Tigers ' game against Florida . The No. 25-ranked Tigers will play No. 8 Florida, which currently ranks No. 5 in the FBS with 532.8 yards of total offense per game, on Saturday in Columbia. Smith and Kitchen were Mizzou's starting defensive ends in each of their first three games of the season, but over the past two game weeks, both players have left the field with injuries and were unable to return. Smith was helped off the field during the first half of Mizzou's Week 3 win over Troy due to an ankle injury. He attempted to return in the second half but only remained on the field for one play. The fifth-year senior did not play in MU's loss at Mississippi State this past Saturday. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of the game against the Bulldogs and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. "Both are doing the very best they can to get back," Drinkwitz said. "I doubt they can participate in much of any practice today (Tuesday), but both of those guys are experienced. You know, our protocol is you have to practice by Thursday in order to be available for the game. Life in the SEC, that's kind of how we go about it with guys who are questionable." The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. picks.blurb: Staff predictions for Virginia vs Florida State — a high-end rematch on deck Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS BB To keep pace and maintain a tie for first place in the ACC, Virginia must conquer Florida State in its first true road game of 2026. An ACC road game is never easy — but the Cavaliers are actually favored to pick up a win at the feared Doak Campbell Stadium. Here are game predictions from the Virginia On SI staff: Jackson Caudell: Virginia 31, Florida State 21 I think this is going to be an interesting test for UVA. While FSU and West Virginia are not the same team, they pose similar challenges. The Seminoles are a mess, but they have talented running backs and a quarterback who can stress you with his legs, much like WVU. Playing away from Charlottesville has not been kind to Virginia so far this year (though a small sample size), and I think they need to be careful here. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, there are two major factors that make it essentially impossible for Florida State to win. The Seminoles have the ACC's second-worst pass defense through four games — so Virginia should have little trouble scoring 35-plus points. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. The Cavaliers can capitalize on those turnovers by turning them into lengthy touchdown drives. Florida State is capable of making things interesting — especially at home — but there are a few reasons why Virginia is the favorite in an ACC road game. This should be a Cavaliers win by multiple scores. Steve DeShazo: Virginia 27, Florida State 31 Saturday brings Virginia's first true road game of 2026. It comes against a proud and talented team that has not played up to its capabilities and may be competing to save Coach Mike Norvell's job in the same way I believe the Cavaliers did for Elliott last year. FSU's offensive skill trio of quarterback Ashton Daniels, receiver Ousman Kromah and receiver Duce Robinson will be a handful for the Cavaliers to contain. Beau Pribula could have a field day passing against the Seminoles, and it may be mandatory to keep Virginia close. The Cavaliers have yet to win a close game or pull out a victory away from home this season. Their only true test came at Charlotte, where the defense struggled and the offensive line showed some vulnerability in a 38-27 loss to West Virginia. Loading recommendations... Virginia's run defense was great in the three wins, but it couldn't hold down the West Virginia offense in the one loss, allowing close to 250 rushing yards. With the road games at Louisville and Miami coming up, the program needs plenty of positive momentum starting now. The Seminoles will be great for the first 20 minutes, but they won't put Virginia away. The Cavaliers will be efficient, balanced, and effective. They won't make the big mistakes late that FSU will. It will beVirginia's first visit to Tallahassee in over a decade, and the Cavaliers havenot won at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2011. Last season, Florida State droppeda 46-38 decision to the Cavaliers in Charlottesville. BroadcastInformation Date : Oct. 3, 2026 Time : 2:30 PM CDT Location : Doak Campbell Stadium,Tallahassee, Florida BettingOdds : Virginia-2.5-point favorite VirginiaCavaliers Virginia, the2025 ACC runner-up under head coach Tony Elliott, is led on the field byquarterback Beau Pribula. A transfer from Missouri and Penn State, Pribula hasfound early season success with the Cavaliers. Pribula ranks in the top 10 inthe FBS in completion percentage (76.7) and touchdown passes (11) while leading Virginia to averaging 40.5 points per game. Pribulawill challenge a Florida State pass defense that allows 290 yards per gamethrough the air. That is bad enough to rank No. 135 in the FBS. In addition,the Seminoles have intercepted three passes in their four games. TheCavaliers average 192.75 yards per game rushing the football, and will face aSeminoles defense that has allowed 139.75 rushing yards per contest. FloridaState defensive coordinator Tony White told the media, and by extension theVirginia coaching staff , that his team focused on stopping the run this week inpractice. We will see if that focus pays off, because the Seminole defendersare executing defensive play calls with a success rate of around 60 percent,according to White. FloridaState Seminoles The FloridaState offense will face off against a Virginia defense that ranks in the top 20in total defense (247 yards per game), pass defense (130.3 yards per game), andscoring defense (13 points per game). FloridaState quarterback Ashton Daniels has struggled with ball security through fourgames, and has thrown five interceptions. That is an issue that has plaguedDaniels throughout his career. Virginia is tied for No. 5 in the FBS ininterceptions with six, with multiple INTs in two of their four games thisseason. Daniels has thrown six touchdown passes this season. Aneffective strategy against Virginia may be to feed running back Ousmane Kromahthe football as much as possible. Florida State can attack the Cavaliersrushing defense, which has allowed opponents 116.75 yards per game this season.Kromah has averaged 6.20 yards per carry and can pound the Cavaliers intosubmission. Against non-Power4 opponents this season, Virginia allowed less than 100 yards rushing in threegames. However, against West Virginia, the Mountaineers shredded the Cavaliersdefense for 247 rushing yards and three touchdowns. So, Virginia is weakagainst the run at times. Over thepast two seasons, including a loss to SMU this season, Florida State has wonjust three ACC games, with 14 conference losses. Something has to click in themindset of the Seminoles as they come out of the tunnel and onto Bobby BowdenField. All thegood things that happened in practice this week, the execution and the focus, musttranslate into a victory for Florida State. The Seminoles must rise above theircurrent station in their football life and make the war chant and the tomahawk choprelevant again. That relevancy begins with a win on Saturday.

Some games that were previously near-locks (Duke and Wake Forest) are now likely to be high-stakes matchups in the ACC standings. However, the overall outlook remains about the same. ESPN predicts the Cavaliers to go 10-2 (8-1 ACC), which would be enough to earn a spot in the ACC title game as long as three of Miami, Clemson, Pitt and SMU lose at least one or two more ACC games. Here is the game-by-game outlook: At Florida State: 58.4% chance of victory (Previously 53.9%) The Seminoles remain one of the bigger unknowns in the conference. After a brutally frustrating home loss to SMU, Florida State came a few plays away from upsetting Alabama on the road. This week's game is a true tipping point for the Seminoles - and Virginia. Syracuse: 84.3% chance of victory (Prev. 77.3%) Quarterback Steve Angeli has struggled. A lot. His interception total nearly matches his touchdown total, and Syracuse's season might be over before it started. The Orange are in desparate need of a win, more so than just about any other team in the Power Four. At SMU: 45.6% chance of victory (Prev. 34.6%) The Mustangs have looked more like an eight-win team than a Playoff team so far. As a result, this game has gone from near-impossible to a true toss-up. Virginia has an increasingly decent chance to steal the upset in Dallas and take pole position in the ACC title race. Duke: 58.7% chance of victory (Prev. 73.6%) Duke has been one of the bigger positive surprises in the conference. Its offense has picked up where it left off (despite a massive portal exodus), and the defense has taken major strides. Right now, the Blue Devils could very well run the table and return to Charlotte. At Wake Forest: 58.3% chance of victory (Prev 62.5%) Aside from Duke, Wake Forest has been the biggest pleasant surprise in the ACC this year. The Demon Deacons nearly upset No. 4 Miami, and just upset No. 16 Louisville. This Halloween bout looks increasingly dangerous for the Cavaliers. Cal: 90.6% chance of victory (Prev. 90.8%) This number might still be too high. Yes, the Golden Bears have sputtered out of the gate, but there is too much talent on this offense for Cal to be mediocre. North Carolina: 74.1% chance of victory (Prev. 69.8%) Bill Belichick's Tar Heels team is elite defensively. Once again, all questions reside on the offensive side of the ball. Can North Carolina keep pace with Virginia? At Virginia Tech: 53.1% chance of victory (Prev. 49.4%) In a shocking development, the Cavaliers' odds continue to rise in this game. Virginia Tech as a home underdog is a great surprise - but Virginia does have a loaded roster with the ability to steal a win in Blacksburg, Va. Noles247.com staff predictions for Florida State's game versus Virginia at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Fla. on Saturday afternoon: Virginia's defense is a solid, though far from outstanding, unit. But in a game where possessions are going to be limited, I question Florida State's ability to slow down the Cavaliers' offense enough for Ashton Daniels and company to keep up with them, given what they've shown over the first month of the season. That starts in the trenches, where Virginia appears to have a significant advantage over the Seminoles' undersized defensive line. Even if Florida State can come out firing as they did early against Alabama , the Cavaliers will stick to what has brought them success this season and wear down the Seminoles' front as the game rolls into the second half – where they could be hurt by play action from Pribula as the second level gets antsy trying to jump into the backfield. The path to victory for Florida State comes from putting Pribula under the pressure he hasn't faced this season, forcing him into a mistake, and capitalizing with points off a turnover. But between Pribula and Daniels, the latter has been more prone to do so, and when the possession battle will be so important, one of those unforced errors could be costly for the Seminoles' chances of coming away with the victory. I think Florida State's offense will find some success, especially from Ousmane Kromah and the rushing attack. But as the game continues, the Seminoles' defense will struggle to get off the field, and Virginia will control things on the ground on its way to a win in Tallahassee. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 20 I find this to be a particularly interesting matchup as both have multiple ways to win. There a lot of "good vs. bad" matchups for both teams in this game. Virginia's ability to run the ball vs. FSU's 1200 thread count soft run defense. Florida State's skill talent on offense vs. a decidedly mediocre Cavalier secondary. Etc. Etc. The position that I will be the deciding factor is quarterback. Both teams will score, and Virginia will 100% limit the overall possessions by holding onto the ball. That means the importance of every possession is magnified. Every explosive you hit carries that much more weight, but every turnover is catastrophic. It all comes down to which team plays a cleaner game and limits unforced errors. I'm taking Virginia. Prediction: Virginia 34, Florida State 27 Florida State can win this game, but I am not convinced they will. My concerns is that Virginia , led by quarterback Beau Pribula , will find consistent success running into the heart of the FSU defensive line, controlling the game, the clock, and exhausting a defense that lacks capable depth and talent. An offense with the oldest offensive line in the country can control this game and should be able to manufacture multiple clock-eating touchdown drives against a Seminole defense that leaves plenty to be desired. They are efficient through the air, though they aren't built to push it down the field aggressively. My reason for optimism when it comes to the Seminoles is that I find Virginia's defense to be susceptible. In the loss to West Virginia , the Cavaliers struggled with a quarterback who ran at them in key moments, though Michael Hawkins Jr. has more wiggle than Ashton Daniels . A couple physical backs for the Mountaineers found success, too, and I think Ousmane Kromah , who should probably see his heaviest workload of the season, can do the same. Also, Virginia will give opportunities on the outside in 1-on-1 coverage and FSU can win there, specifically Duce Robinson who will likely be very motivated after his performance, which included some tough moments, in Charlottesville last season against UVA. Finally, UVA safety Ethan Minter is a player that can be attacked on the seam or vertically with athletic wide receivers. Game can easily swing via turnovers, and that is an area where Virginia is far better than FSU at not committing them on offense and forcing them on defense. I don't have strong feelings either way with one team being an overwhelming favorite. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 28 I've gone back and forth on this game. To be honest both teams are mediocre middle to bottom half of the ACC caliber teams right now. Both quarterbacks leave a lot to be desired. The skill on defense is not up to snuff with years past for either program. That being said, UVA does possess the better offensive line while FSU has the superior skill talent. What does all of that mean? Well it's going to be a battle of styles. Florida States passing attack against UVAs rushing attack. FSU must find explosive wins in the passing game at a more consistent rate while UVA tries to control the ball with a high success rate rushing attack. If Ashton Daniels can be aggressive against the man looks UVA will show him then FSU can win this game. If Ashton Daniels is passive this is going to get ugly in a hurry. I'm going to try a bit of optimism… Prediction: Florida State 34, Virginia 27 Kolby Crawford Everything is telling me to pick Virginia. Bad roster construction up front on both sides, an undersized line that can't hold up against a team built to run right at you, a season already bleeding attendance and goodwill. Which is exactly why I think Norvell comes out with a great plan and jumps on them early at home. Call it surprise, call it vibes, whatever it is, I feel it this week. I still believe this season takes a downturn fast from here, but this is one of the last wins they scrape out before it does. Slang that thing, Ashton. Prediction: Florida State 27, Virginia 23 Virginia had a promising start to the season but that loss to WVU in pretty convincing style is starting to negatively shape my perception of this team. To me the eyes test doesn't bear out against the advanced analytics. F+ has them as a top 25 defense and not a top 25 offense. That doesn't really track with what I see. Their offense is plodding and efficient. They use their mobile QB well, get their 3-4 yards a pop with a well structured IZ scheme, and then work for shots over the top off of play action. Think our offense from last year but without Duce and maybe a more consistent QB. Their defense struggled against WVU. To be honest, they looked good against NCSU but my middle school flag football team could look good against a Dave Doeren offense. Their secondary seems a bit slow and I think if you can spring into the second level you can rip off some chunks. They have a solid front six though which they try to lean on but I think FSU can find some success getting Duce and Kromah outside. This will be a dog fight in my estimation but I gotta give the benefit to the QB I trust more. picks.blurb: Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Virginia | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 2, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looking to get to .500 in ACC action for first time since 2023 Florida State hosts the Virginia Cavaliers for the first time since 2014, a 34-20 Seminole win, on Saturday at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m., and the game will be televised on ESPN2. Of the 21 meetings between FSU and UVA, Saturday marks only the third time (2006, 2010, 2026) that neither team is ranked in the Associated Press Top 25. Florida State (2-2, 0-1 ACC) and the Cavaliers (3-1, 1-0 ACC) will meet for the second straight season and the 21st time overall in UVA’s first true road game of the ‘26 season. FSU and UVA have not met in back-to-back seasons since the 2010 and 2011 seasons, with FSU holding a 15-5 all-time record against UVA, including a 9-1 record at Doak. Virginia’s only victory came in 2011 when the Wahoos defeated the then-No. 23 Seminoles, 14-13. UVA will be trying for its third consecutive win and fourth in its last five meetings with the Noles. Saturday will be a rematch of last year’s double-overtime loss by then-No. 8 FSU in Charlottesville, which ended with a game-sealing interception in the end zone by the Cavaliers. The victory was UVA’s first over a top-10 opponent at home since defeating then-No. 4 Florida State 26-21 in 2005. Virginia’s defense comes into the contest allowing just 130 passing yards per game, the fifth-fewest in the nation and the lowest in the ACC, and ranked 14th in total defense, giving up just 247 yards per game. Opposing quarterbacks sport an 84.2 efficiency rating, the lowest in the country. UVA is one of 20 FBS teams allowing fewer than 14 points per game. The Cavaliers have held two of its four opponents without a touchdown and only allowed a total of 52 points on the season. On offense, UVA quarterback Beau Pribula ranks fifth nationally in passing efficiency (194.1), with 11 touchdown passes, tying for seventh in the country, and tied for fourth in the ACC. Eighteen Cavaliers have caught a pass this season, and each of UVA’s last three games has featured double-digit pass catchers. Pribula has completed 66 of 86 passes and ranks fourth in the nation with a 77% completion percentage. The Seminoles are coming off their second win of the season after unimpressively beating outmanned Central Arkansas, 34-7. The Noles went 4-for-4 in the Red Zone against Central Arkansas and are now 17-for-17 to begin the 2026 season. FSU’s 17 Red Zone conversions are the 4th most in the country among the 19 teams that are still perfect inside the 20. Jayvan Boggs, Seminoles coast past Central Arkansas to get back to .500 FSU QB Ashton Daniels is 58-of-97 passing for 928 yards and six touchdowns, with 142 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns. He has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all four games. Daniels is the only player in FBS in 2026 with multiple rushing and passing touchdowns and a two-point conversion. On the season, the Noles’ offense is ranked a not-so-nice 69th in total offense, 76th in the nation in 3rd down conversions with just a 40.8% rate on 20-of-49 attempts, and tied for 63rd in scoring offense with a 32-point average per game. FSU’s 126th-ranked total defense is allowing 430 total yards per game, 290 passing yards per game (135th out of 138 FBS teams), and ranked 121st in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert almost 46% of the time on third-down attempts. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Virginia Cavaliers Florida State is trending as a 2.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 51.5 points according to FanDuel. Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Curt Weiler (season record: 4-0, 2-2 ATS) Considering FSU’s defensive problems against talented teams this season, it’s hard to predict the success will begin against a Virginia offense, which has thrown 15 touchdowns to one interception this season while rushing for nearly 200 yards per game. And that doesn’t even factor in a Virginia defense which is second in the ACC in yards per play allowed (4.1) on a team that has a plus-five turnover differential this season. FSU will need its home-field advantage to work overtime to make up for what feels like a talent discrepancy, as wild as that is to say considering Virginia has won at Doak Campbell Stadium exactly one time. Virginia 31, Florida State 24 Matt Minnick (season record: 4-0, 3-1 ATS) This game is FSU’s season. A win on Saturday and the ‘Noles move to 1-1 in ACC play and a chance to really establish some momentum the following week with a suddenly vulnerable Louisville squad. Lose to UVA, and it becomes hard to see Florida State avoiding a tailspin that results in a 3-9 type season. When you look at the advanced stats, Florida State’s offense is respectable in many areas. It’s still a small sample size, but adjusted for SOS, the ‘Noles have the 18th best offense overall according to FEI, better than Nebraska, Texas, UCLA, LSU, SMU, Louisville, Virginia Tech, UVA, and a host of other teams with better records. Buoying the FSU offense are their explosive plays, ranking 36th in points per drive and 38th in yards per play. However, there is one area FSU’s offense really struggles in, and that is “busted drive rate” where the ‘Noles rank 90th. A “busted drive” is defined as a drive that gains 0 or fewer net yards, and here in lies Florida State’s biggest problem. FSU’s boom and bust offense does a nice job of putting points on the board in bunches, but when you have a defense that cannot get off the field (even when playing inferior opponents), it is essential that you consistently sustain success on offense. Otherwise, every busted drive results in your opponent receiving better and better field position and chewing up more and more of the clock. Not playing complementary football has been a theme under Norvell, and thus far this season is no exception. Virginia’s defense admittedly has not faced a murderer’s row, but they rank 13th in defensive busted drive rate. If the busted drive trends for both teams hold, it’s hard to see Florida State emerging victorious. But if FSU can find a way to limit their three and outs and turnovers, the Seminoles might be able to hit enough explosives to outscore the ‘Hoos at home. For the second time this season, FSU finds itself a short underdog at home, a typical “sharp spot” for betters in Vegas. Similar to the SMU game, I think FSU has its chances but just can’t quite find a way to get the W. UVA 35, FSU 34 Jordan Silversmith (season record: 4-0) Last year’s loss to Virginia turned Florida State’s season sideways at a pivotal moment. Saturday will do the same thing. UVA is favored by Vegas — on the road — because they are the better team. The Cavs are the most experienced squad in the country and have an identity on both sides of the ball. Meanwhile, Florida State is still finding itself. On offense, they are boom-or-bust, producing explosive plays on the ground and through the air but unable to sustain drives. Defensively, FSU’s defensive coordinator Tony White apologized to the offense after the Central Arkansas game for letting the Bears hold the ball for 40 minutes of time of possession. That says all that anyone needs to know about where the Seminoles are on that side of the ball. Even if FSU technically has better players, as Virginia is ranked 57th in 247Sports’ Talent Composite, UVA has the better, coach, quarterback, and knows how to win. Virginia wins and covers. UVA 31, FSU 27 NoleThruandThru (season record: 4-0) I’m just here so I don’t get fined. FSU 31, Virginia 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 3-0) All week I’ve been setting up how this is a bad match-up for FSU and how the more experienced, better coach, better quarterback, and better match-up UVA team should win, so naturally I’m going with the ‘Noles. Boom or bust offenses work better at home than on the road, and this is UVA’s first true road test of the year, as their only game away from the comforts of Charlottesville so far was a neutral-site loss to West Virginia. FSU 28, UVA 27 Jon Marchant (season record: 2-0 ) Virginia’s Beau Pribula is very good at keeping Virginia ahead of the chains, whether it’s with quick passes or his legs. However, if you can get Virginia into obvious passing downs, that’s where he struggles. Unfortunately for FSU, the Noles’ defense is terrible on passing downs, so I don’t think it’s a good matchup for FSU as far as that side of the ball goes. Meanwhile, the Seminoles’ offense is very boom or bust—if they hit an explosive play, they have a chance to score. It’s inherently an inconsistent way to play offense and means you will get a wide range of results from game to game. Does FSU have a chance in this game? Yes; it depends on 1) whether the defense can get even one or two stops and 2) how many explosive plays the offense can connect on. It’s just not very likely. Virginia 34, FSU 24 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-0 ) Virginia’s offensive line is one of the very best and most experienced in the country, with several guys at their 5th+ year. I have no doubt that Beau Pribula, a man who’s stat line has him tied for 7th in the nation for touchdowns, is going to absolutely tear up the Noles defense. FSU will mount a comeback attempt late, but it will be fruitless. Virginia 33, FSU 19 Tim Scribble (season record: 4-0) I think we could see a similar game to last year’s loss by Florida State. A shootout at times with Virginia pulling away. UVA 38, FSU 27 Tony Morris (season record: 2-0) It is time to right the ship (hopefully). Sit back and watch this Ous and Wisner masterclass of 200+ rushing yards. This simply comes down to if the defense can get the stops (even if it’s just a couple). FSU’s offense will do its part. Noles 31, Cavs 24 Frank DaNole (season record: 2-2) This will be the game when everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are only 2.5-point underdogs for a reason. Vegas knows it, and the Seminoles know it. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed last year when Alabama came to Tallahassee. The Seminoles may not dominate at all three positional units for the entire game, but in the end FSU will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their more talented, deeper, and better coached UVA opponents. There’s nothing in the body of work that the Seminoles have put together through four games that have me confident they’ll buck the concerning trends they’ve exhibited. Virginia might not have had too many tests so far (failing one already), but the Cavaliers have taken care of business when needed. FSU has not, failing to show any sort of consistent success on either sid

home.headline: Updated week 5 injury report adds to a growing issue within Florida State's defense
home.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. The updated injury report delivered a few positive bits of news for Florida State, as Ashlynd Barker, Chris Jones, KJ Kirkland, Donny Hiebert, and Xavier Tiller were all upgraded

The season is on the verge of running off the tracks and the result of this game could smooth things out for another week or completely derail the entire season. Who comes out on top in a battle between former SEC East foes? South Carolina is in the midst of an eight game losing streak to Power Four opponents, which includes seven losses to SEC teams. During this losing streak Beamer's Gamecocks have fallen to Alabama (twice), LSU, Oklahoma, Mississippi State, Texas A&M, and Ole Miss. Their last win came against Kentucky in a 35-13 route of the Wildcats. However now with Will Stein at the helm, this is not the same Kentucky team of recent years. Wildcats QB Kenny Minchey and this offense have been very efficient and moved the ball well. They got a statement win earlier in the year at College Station and are looking for another. What may help South Carolina in this one is Kentucky's leaky defense . The Wildcats rank 14th in scoring (25 ppg), 12th in rushing (122.25 yards per game), and 13th against the pass (234 yards per game). Rain may be in the forecast for this weekend. This very well could play right into the Gamecocks' hands as they have a much improved rushing attack from last season. With that said, I believe the Gamecocks are in for a bounce back spot on Saturday. Kentucky's defense will give up plays through the air and on the ground. Kendal Briles should be able to mix up the play calling well and allow LaNorris Sellers to get into a groove. Matt Fuller has topped the 100-yard mark twice in the last three games. I believe he hits that number once again and officially puts a bad losing streak to an end. Joey Walraven: South Carolina 24, Kentucky 21 This game is a must-win for the South Carolina Gamecocks. A loss here could potentially be cement another losing season for the Gamecocks and be the final touches on Shane Beamer's exit . With those implications, I expect LaNorris Sellers to have his best game of the season and lead the Gamecocks to a hard fought victory. Sellers will cetainly need to play well, but the difference in this game will be on the ground. The Gamecocks boast the best rushing attack in the SEC as well as allowing the fourth fewest average yards of on the ground in the conference. Loading recommendations... picks.headline: Three bold predictions for when the South Carolina Gamecocks take on Kentucky
picks.blurb: Despite all the troubles from the last two weeks, South Carolina has a chance to get the train back on the track against Kentucky. For a team desparately needing a win, here are three bold predicitions for the Gamecocks that will ultimately end their 2-game skid this season. Usually we try to give you at least one on each side of the ball, however this week we're changing things up. This is an all offense version of bold predictions. We will focus on LaNorris Sellers, the passing game, and the tailbacks. Passing Game looks smooth again It certainly won't be easy. Though Knetucky's "stats" place them in the bottom half of SEC defenses in the passing category, it doesn't tell the full story. In two SEC games the Wildcats held Alabama's Keelon Russell to 188 yards passing and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed to 236 yards. They also lead the conference in interceptions with 6. What gives me confidence in this specific matchup will be South Carolina's ability to run the ball (more on that later). A good run game can open passing windows for an offense that has struggled in that department for the last two weeks. I expect this to be the case and for Gamecocks to see a better attack than they have in recent weeks. LaNorris Sellers finishes with no interceptions In the last three games, Sellers has four interceptions , two of which came against Mississippi State. On the other side, Kentucky has been great this season at creating turnovers. On paper this is a matchup that favors the Wildcats. However I believe Seller ends his interception streak this week and keeps this passing game on track. Gamecocks rush for 200+ In their two SEC games this season, Kentucky gave up 155 yards and three touchdowns to Bama. Against Texas A&M they gave up 187 yards and two touchdowns. This is a front seven that can be run on and that's exactly what this Gamecocks' offense does best. Matt Fuller leads a rushing attack that is ranked first in the conference with 262 yards per game. Fuller gained 112 yards on the ground last week as the team put up 216 yards total on Alabama. Against Mississippi State running backs totaled 149 yards. That's good enough for 182.5 yards per game through two contests. Fuller should have his third 100 yard rushing performance of the season which will propel the Gamecocks to a win. picks.blurb: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats have to go on their second road trip of the season as the will face off against South Carolina at 4:15 P.M. ET on Saturday. We have previewed both South Carolina offense and defense, as well as laying out Kentucky's path to victory in this game. This is a massive game for both teams; Kentucky is trying to snap a four game losing streak against the Gamecocks and South Carolina is a desperate trying to turnaround their season. In this article, I will give my final thoughts on the game and a prediction. Kentucky has to win early downs in this game, and they have consistently done that all season on both sides of the football. Kentucky's offense has stayed ahead of schedule consistently and haven't needed to rely on converting third downs, which has been a weak spot for this offense. Kentucky's offensive line has improved every week and they have to dominate the line of scrimmage in this game. They have been phenomenal in run blocking as they lead the country in yards before contact per rush attempt, and they should keep Kenny Minchey clean as South Carolina is without their game-wrecking edge defender Dylan Stewart. Defensively, Kentucky has performed similarly as the offense. They are struggling on third downs, but they have been exceptional on early downs. If they can slow down this South Carolina run game and keep their offense off schedule, it should bode well for the Wildcats defense. Kentucky will probably have a similar defensive gameplan that they had against Texas A&M, contain LaNorris Sellers on the ground and force him to beat you with his arm. Sellers has struggled this season, he has turned the ball over four times. The turnover margin has been the downfall of Kentucky in this series as of late, as the Wildcats have 14 total turnovers in the last five matchups against the Gamecocks. That could flip on Saturday, Kentucky is +3 in the turnover margin on the season, whereas South Carolina is -4 in the turnover margin. Kentucky has done a great job at taking care of the football and creating turnovers on defense. South Carolina has their backs against the wall, head coach Shane Beamer is on a scorching hot seat. They have struggled against SEC opponents and the talk surrounding their program has been extremely loud this week. Combine that with your best player serving a suspension, it will be a lot to overcome for the Gamecocks. Who gets off to a hot start could be the determining factor in this football game. Speaking of hot starts, there are multiple reasons it could play a factor in this game. South Carolina needs to create that early momentum to keep the crowd involved. If Kentucky gets off to a hot start and the Gamecocks struggle offensively, you could see the boo birds come out in Columbia from this fan base. It is worth noting, Kentucky ranks third in the SEC this season in time trailing this season, as the Wildcats have only spent a total of over 26 minutes trailing through the first month of play. Kentucky has been good at getting off to quick starts this season, and I could see that continue on Saturday. Kentucky has a unique offensive scheme that will force a struggling South Carolina defense to communicate. Over the last five meetings, the Wildcats have averaged just 13 points per game, which is the main reason they have been 1-4 over that stretch. I believe Kentucky gets the offense going and South Carolina fails to overcome all the noise surrounding the team this week. Mark Stoops was fired in December after 13 seasons and Will Stein is now leading the program. He was hired out of Oregon where he was the offensive coordinator. South Carolina 's last SEC win was more than a year ago vs Kentucky for a seven-game conference losing streak. Kickoff is 4:15 p.m. on Oct. 3 (SEC Network) in Williams-Brice Stadium . picks.headline: Analytics predict the winner between #24 Kentucky and South Carolina
picks.blurb: Analytics predict the winner between #24 Kentucky and South Carolina - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Analytics predict the winner between #24 Kentucky and South Carolina Kentucky Matt Stein comes out onto the field against Youngstown State at Kroger Field.Sept. 5, 2026 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Andrew Stefaniak Wed, September 30, 2026 at 4:08 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Big Blue Nation has been thrilled by the start of the Will Stein era as his team is ranked #24 in college football four games into the season. The Wildcats are 3-1 and have a big-time road upset as they took down the Texas A&M Aggies, who were ranked #9 at the time. While the hype and excitement are there, the Wildcats have a big-time game on Saturday on the road against the South Carolina Gamecocks. The Gamecocks are 2-2 so far this season, with losses to Alabama and Mississippi State. Fans in Columbia are starting to get really frustrated with the way this team is playing, and some feel that the end could be near for Shane Beamer. Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer reacts to a play during the first quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If the Wildcats are able to win this game, it could be bad for Beamer, and the administration at South Carolina could have a big decision to make. It's clear that Kentucky winning this game would be huge for the Wildcats chances of winning a Bowl Game. ESPN's Matchup Predictor does not like the Wildcats chances of going on the road and taking down the Gamecocks. ESPN only gives the Wildcats a 42.1% chance to go on the road and take down the Gamecocks. South Carolina has taken some ugly losses early in the season, but they still have a lot of talent on this roster. The Gamecocks have a very good quarterback in LaNorris Sellers, who has given Kentucky issues during his time in Columbia. If the Wildcats aren't able to bottle up Sellers, he could give the Cats problems once again. Sellers is a quarterback who can use his legs and arm to beat a team. Kentucky needs to keep containment and make sure he stays in the pocket. If he gets outside of the pocket, this is where he can hurt teams. Sep 26, 2026; Lexington, Kentucky, USA; Kentucky Wildcats head coach Will Stein looks on during the third quarter against the South Alabama Jaguars at Kroger Field. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This feels like a game that Mark Stoops would struggle in, so BBN is hoping that with Stein in charge, things are going to go a lot better in Columbia for the Wildcats. If they do win, a massive game will be set up between the Wildcats and LSU Tigers, with the Power K making a return. This is a big weekend for both Stein and Beamer, but Kentucky fans are hoping the Wildcats will be heading back home with a big-time win. If Kentucky wins, Stein has a great shot at making a year-one bowl. picks.headline: Kentucky vs South Carolina Prediction: Can the Gamecocks Change the Vibe?
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs South Carolina Prediction: Can the Gamecocks Change the Vibe? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Kentucky vs South Carolina Prediction: Can the Gamecocks Change the Vibe? Pete Fiutak Fri, October 2, 2026 at 8:18 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's early October, but it's do-or-die time for a South Carolina (2-2) team that's been a massive disappointment so far. Losing at home to Mississippi State was bad, getting rocked 49-18 at Alabama wasn't fun, and if there's an 0-3 start after a loss to Kentucky (3-1) … Gamecock head coach Shane Beamer almost certainly won't be whacked with a loss, but it'll put the pressure on to be almost perfect the rest of the way against a brutal schedule. Meanwhile, the Wildcats are looking to keep improving. They also got thumped by Alabama, losing 45-17, but they shocked Texas A&M 31-21 and can come up with the best start since 2023 with a win in Columbia. Kentucky vs South Carolina: Quick Hits South Carolina has won four straight in the series, including a 35-13 blowout last year. Kentucky has to deal with LSU after this before going to Oklahoma. South Carolina travels to Florida next, and then it gets a week off to get ready for Tennessee. How To Watch Kentucky vs South Carolina Date: Saturday, October 3, 2026 Game Time: 4:15 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia, SC – Week 5 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 5 – 10 Best Picks Against the Spread Why Kentucky Will Win What's South Carolina's problem? To get weird and groovy here, there's a general negativity thing happening. The Mississippi State loss threw the program for a loop (the same thing happened at Minnesota). Getting rocked at Alabama is getting rocked at Alabama – welcome to life in the SEC, son. But the way Mississippi State beat the Gamecocks didn't seem to sit well, considering that was supposed to be a sure-thing win when looking at the schedule in the preseason. Kentucky was tied 7-7 with Texas A&M at halftime, and carried the positive momentum to a 28-point run in the shocker in College Station. A few early scores might trigger the South Carolina negative chi after losing seven straight SEC games going back to last year. (Sorry, I'm done with that now.) Why South Carolina Will Win Third down conversions. Kentucky can't get them on offense and can't stop them on defense. It's among the worst teams in America on both sides, converting just 23% of its chances, and allowing teams to convert 45% of their tries. It did a good job last week against South Alabama, but Alabama and Texas A&M were able to keep the chains moving without a problem. South Carolina has to get its great running game going, set up easy third down tries, and keep its struggling defense on the sidelines. Kentucky vs South Carolina Prediction, Betting Lines Again with the Mississippi State thing. The Bulldogs are good, Alabama is great, and South Carolina is about to show that it's good, too, and those two losses weren't nearly as bad, and things aren't as dire, as many might make it seem. It won't be easy, but the Gamecocks will run their way to a gut-check win. away.blurb: South Carolina will have a lot of pressure on them Saturday, while Kentucky wants to get one step closer to bowl game eligibility. With the matchup on the horizon, the injury report was released on Wednesday night. How are things looking? As Will Stein noted on Tuesday, Kentucky has a couple of guys currently questionable, but DJ Miller has popped up as 'Doubtful', who Stein has said has been dealing with a soft tissue, which bothered the sophomore against South Alabama. "There'll be some guys that are questionable for this weekend," Stein said when asked about injuries on Tuesday. "Nothing I would say is season ending or that's going to be more than a game. But I'm expecting to be almost at full health (against South Carolina). ...Hopefully by Saturday, we're up to as full strength as we can be." away.headline: Initial Injury Report for Kentucky at South Carolina
away.blurb: A big name on the injury report is wide receiver DJ Miller, who is dealing with a soft tissue injury that caused him to just play eight snaps against South Alabama. He is listed as doubtful. Miller had a breakout game against Texas A&M and has been the second best wideout behind true freshman Kenny Darby. He has dealt with soft tissue injuries throughout his young career at Kentucky, he was sidelined last season as a true freshman because of it and dealt with something similar this offseason as well. This is certainly something to monitor. Other than Miller, Jordan Castell is the other starter listed, but he is probable, so not a big worry. Ty Bryant, the other starting safety, isn't listed on the report despite dealing with a shoulder injury over the past few weeks. Outside of Dylan Stewart serving a suspension, South Carolina is pretty healthy across the board. There aren't many notable names on this list for the Gamecocks. Defensive lineman Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy is questionable, and the other potential key player out of action. Kentucky could be slightly undermanned in this road test that is a massive game for both teams. These injury reports will continue to be updated throughout the week, but the initial injury report suggests Kentucky could potentially be down a couple key starters on Saturday. Obviously, nothing is more notable than South Carolina being without star edge rusher Dylan Stewart , who is currently serving a suspension after throwing a punch against Alabama last weekend. Kentucky is relatively healthy, but there are key starters that are listed. Kentucky has stayed relatively healthy so far this season, but we will continue to monitor who might be sidelined for the Wildcats in this SEC matchup. away.headline: Georgia Southern turns to Sun Belt play after three straight losses
away.blurb: Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) Eagles open conference play at Coastal Carolina with a 1-3 record, plus key injury updates following Saturday’s loss to No. 25 Houston. Georgia Southern is ready to turn the page. The Eagles enter Sun Belt play at 1-3 after dropping three straight games, including Saturday’s 42-28 loss to No. 25 Houston at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Despite the loss, Georgia Southern showed some encouraging signs offensively. Quarterback Max Johnson turned in his strongest performance of the season, completing 26 of 38 passes for 284 yards and a season-high three touchdowns without an interception. The Eagles also continued to expand the role of quarterback Weston Bryan. Georgia Southern used packages featuring both quarterbacks on the field together, including a flea-flicker that started with Bryan and ended with Johnson finding Alex Taylor for a 40-yard touchdown. Taylor finished with a season-high 119 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Southern now turns its attention to conference play while also dealing with several injuries. Head coach Clay Helton confirmed Monday that wide receiver Ashton Hollins will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery. Hollins, an Illinois transfer, suffered the injury in the Eagles’ loss at Jacksonville State. Inside linebacker Rashon Myles Jr. also left Saturday’s game against Houston with an Achilles injury. Helton said Myles was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday to determine the extent of the injury. The Eagles were also without two starting offensive tackles against Houston because of illness. Helton said neither had been medically cleared to play. Georgia Southern will now look to regroup as the Sun Belt portion of its schedule begins. The Eagles have lost three straight, while Coastal Carolina enters the matchup at 1-3 and riding a two-game losing streak. Both teams now look for a fresh start, 0-0 in conference play. Saturday will also mark Georgia Southern’s first matchup against the Chanticleers under first-year Coastal Carolina head coach Ryan Beard. The Eagles have won three straight games in the series, including a 26-6 victory in their last trip to Conway in 2024. Georgia Southern leads the all-time series 8-4. Georgia Southern and Coastal Carolina kick off Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7 p.m. from Brooks Stadium in Conway, South Carolina. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the biggest ACC games of the season takes place Saturday night as No. 4 Miami heads to Death Valley to take on Clemson . Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender. (Patrick Breen/The Republic) 1 / 29 Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney How much of this game will have to be decided by Reynolds, who is a freshman? This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Clemson vs. Miami scouting report Where Clemson has an advantage: Miami hasn't faced a secondary as good as Clemson's. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Where Miami has an advantage: The Hurricanes look better at the line of scrimmage. Miami ranks second in the ACC with 227.5 rushing yards per game, and running backs Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher Jr. are averaging 9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. Miami also looks better on the other side. Marquise Lightfoot is tied for fourth in the ACC with four sacks, while Damon Wilson II and Armondo Blount can win one-on-one. Miami generated pressure on 60.8% of Wake Forest's dropbacks in its last ACC game, and Reynolds is 20 of 46 for 175 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions when he's under pressure or blitzed. picks.headline: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire?
picks.blurb: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Sam Navarro-Imagn Images; Ken Ruinard-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 1, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Canes and Tigers will have the eyes of the nation on them on Saturday night in a big game for two programs going in different directions. The Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers square off on Saturday night in Death Valley in a game with significant ACC title implications, with the game being shown in primetime on ABC. The Canes have surged to a 4-0 start, with only a slight flutter in the second half at Wake Forest after leading 31-7 being their only show of mortality thus far. Meanwhile, Clemson has improved to 3-1 after a season-opening 51-10 loss at LSU. Lifeless performances against Georgia Southern and in the first half against UNC have turned into a come from behind win over the Tar Heels and an impressive 24-10 win at Cal last weekend. Can the Tigers ride that modest improvement into an upset win on Saturday night? Our college football writers weighed in with their game predictions. Miami 38, Clemson 28 I think the writing is on the wall for Clemson and Dabo Swinney. The program is a shell of itself, esepcially from a talent acquisition standpoint. Things are the exact opposite for the Hurricanes, as they were less than 70 yards away from a national championship. Even so, I expect Clemson to show out for this game almost as a last ditch effort to save their season. It won't be enough, as the Hurricanes prove to be too explosive for the Tigers. Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida Miami 30, Clemson 10 This game had the potential to be one of the better matchups in the ACC this season if Clemson held up their end of the bargain, but it looks like Dabo and the boys have only fallen further down the list in terms of program competence. The quarterback position is a mess, and a lot of the notable draft prospects heading into the season simply haven't played up to the offseason hype. On the other hand, you have a Miami team with not only one of the sport's most explosive weapons in Malachi Toney, but also one of the most efficient passers in college football in Darian Mensah. I know Clemson is at home, but this has a chance to be a route for the Hurricanes. Give me Miami, big. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Miami 34, Clemson 21 This game is much closer than the final score suggests, with Clemson hanging around for a large portion of the afternoon. One of the biggest storylines will be how the Tigers handle Malachi Toney. It'll be interesting to see if Clemson allows CB Ashton Hampton to follow Toney around the field and essentially shadow him, considering Hampton is the most talented defensive back Miami has faced to this point. If Clemson can limit Toney and force Miami to win elsewhere, the Tigers have a chance to make this uncomfortable. Ultimately, though, Miami's overall talent takes over as the game progresses. The Hurricanes make enough explosive plays on offense to create separation, while Clemson capitalizes on a couple of coverage busts from the Miami secondary for some big plays of its own. Miami's depth and playmakers prove to be the difference in the second half, allowing the Hurricanes to pull away and finish with a 34-21 victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame Miami 30, Clemson 13 This feels like a game that could be closer than many pundits are giving it credit for, and perhaps those in Las Vegas as well. The 17-point line feels out of place for what Clemson has been over the last decade, but Dabo Swinney's Tigers have looked anything but the part of contenders the last few years. Clemson's secondary is talented, led by Ashton Hampton, who could play himself into first round consideration in April's NFL Draft. I could see the Tigers giving Miami's offense problems and preventing some of the chunk plays that Miami has ripped off all year with the exception of a quarter and a half against Wake Forest. But Clemson freshman QB Tait Reynolds is going to have a rough experience against a Miami team that's starting to get a tad healthier on the defensive side of the ball. DL Ahmad Moten, Sr. and Armondo Blount are off the injury report and appear set to be available on Saturday, along with CB Damari Brown. Starting CB Xavier Lucas could even possibly be in play, but even if not, Ethan O'Connor has been one of the better CBs in the ACC this year and can handle things very capably. Miami slowly puts this one away in the second half with Mark Fletcher, Jr., who is also off the injury report, pounding away in the fourth quarter on a tired defense. UM's last win at Clemson was a 30-21 victory in 2010. Clemson (3-1, 2-0) was throttled by LSU, 51-10, in the season opener and the Tigers have responded with three straight wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, and California.
