away.headline: Miami injury report: Is Malachi Toney playing vs Central Michigan?
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Miami won at Wake Forest, but it cost them dearly. And with injuries limiting Heisman contender Malachi Toney and taking punishing running back Mark Fletcher Jr. out of the game, Hurricanes fans are hoping the extra day off means they're back and ready to play their normal snaps today against Central Michigan . Toney was seen warming up with the receivers and is expected to play Saturday vs. Central Michigan. If he is unavailable, Miami will rely on Daylyn Upshaw and Cooper Barkate as the primary receiving options, meaning CMU can focus more on underneath coverage. Fletcher remained in sweats while his teammates suited up before the game. Multiple reporters, including the Miami Herald's Jordan McPherson , indicated it's likely Fletcher sits. Adam Lichtenstein of the South Florida Sun-Sentinel confirmed he and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten, also injured in the Wake Forest game, would sit out against Central Michigan. If he is unavailable, Miami will switch to a more speed-based running attack with Girard Pringle Jr. with freshman Javian Mallory as the power back. CMU would likely focus more on containing Darian Mensah and the passing game. Who benefits if Malachi Toney is out vs Central Michigan? If Toney is out, Daylyn Upshaw and Cooper Barkate become the primary wide options with more focus funneled toward tight end Elija Lofton. Expect more snaps to Vandrevius Jacobs and freshmen Vance Spafford and Somourian Wingo, as well. Who benefits if Mark Fletcher is out vs Central Michigan? The Canes' leading receiver, second in the nation with 28 catches for 444 yards and tied for fourth with five touchdowns, was used sparingly after that as Darian Mensah and the offense stagnated. Part of that was the subsequent loss of Fletcher, who left during the fourth quarter with an upper-body injury . The senior is Miami's leading rusher with 230 yards and three TDs on 36 carries. Without them and other key offensive pieces, the Canes had to scrap to hold on for the 33-20 win. away.headline: Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury
away.blurb: MIAMI, Fla. – After missing last Saturday's 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium, the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes are set for the return of running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. (both seniors) against Clemson , but it should be taken with caution. The backfield supporting cast suffered a difficult loss of redshirt junior CharMar "Marty" Brown, who is out for the rest of the season with a severe right knee injury, which was sustained against Wake Forest on Sept. 18. He was the primary backup to Fletcher Jr., but an opportunity for more snaps presents itself. For starters, Fletcher Jr. shouldn't return to a heavy workload. As the Hurricanes' go-to running back, the 21-year-old's long-term availability is valuable. Fletcher Jr. proved to turn things up a notch when the lights got brighter in last year's historic run to the National Championship game. Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Anthony Aguirre Wed, September 30, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As the Fort Lauderdale (Fla.) native is inserted back into the mix, it would be beneficial to make it an emphasis to play sophomore Girard Pringle Jr. , freshman Javian Mallory, and redshirt sophomore Chris Wheatley-Humphrey more. Plus, Pringle Jr., Mallory, and Wheatley-Humphrey can gain experience playing college football in a hostile environment. Memorial Stadium, otherwise known as Death Valley, is one of the sport's most historic venues. Pringle Jr. only logged six snaps in last year's College Football Playoffs and Wheatley-Humphrey had 19, but only on special teams. As Hurricanes offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson looks to spread the workload in the backfield, this Saturday presents an opportunity to play at least four different running backs. They will be facing Clemson 's junior linebacker, Sammy Brown , who was the ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. Moten Sr. is off to a slow start this season. Thus far, in 91 snaps across three games, he's logged three total tackles, a solo and two assists, 0.5 tackles for loss, 0.5 sacks, and four pressures. Moten Sr. suffered a left shoulder injury against Wake Forest, left early, then returned to play the rest of the game. Despite having first-round projections in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Hurricanes still need the star defender healthy in the long run. It presents an opportunity for sophomore Jarquez Carter and junior Keona Davis, who have been serviceable in reserve roles, to step up. The Hurricanes have great depth at both running back and defensive tackle. The ACC released its initial availability report for Saturday's game, listing seven Clemson players as out and two as questionable. More importantly, multiple Tigers who recently dealt with injuries were out of the report as a whole. Starting nickelback Corian Gipson , defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and quarterback Christopher Vizzina were not listed as either out or questionable, indicating that all three are available to play against the Hurricanes. Gipson missed Clemson's 24-10 victory over California after being limited to two defensive snaps against North Carolina . Head coach Dabo Swinney confirmed Tuesday that Gipson had returned to practice but stopped short of guaranteeing his availability. "We'll see, but he's practicing," Swinney said. "So, we'll find out today. He practiced last night, so we'll see." Starting left guard Elyjah Thurmon and defensive end Armon Mason are Clemson's two questionable players. Thurmon left the Cal game after 17 snaps and did not return. Gavin Blanchard replaced him at left guard and played the final 57 offensive snaps. Clemson listed seven players as out: Miami listed six players as out: Hurricanes cornerback Xavier Lucas and linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. are questionable. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. , who had both been dealing with injuries, were not listed and are expected to play. home.blurb: Clemson quarterback Christopher Vizzina (right) injured his left elbow against Georgia Southern, but coach Dabo Swinney (left) said Vizzina will still be available vs. North Carolina. Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina is available, coach Dabo Swinney said, but not 100 percent recovered from a small fracture in his left elbow. What’s the Tigers’ plan if they need a backup to play vs. Miami? Clemson listed Vizzina as a game-time decision in the final availability report before Clemson’s Sept. 19 win over North Carolina. He was left off the final report entirely before the Sept. 25 win at Cal. He was listed as Clemson’s backup quarterback on the depth chart vs. Miami, per team release. Top Story Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan By Jackson Castellano jcastellano@postandcourier.com Jackson Castellano Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said Vizzina is throwing and practicing after sustaining a small left elbow fracture Sept. 12 against Georgia Southern. However, Swinney said that Trent Pearman would be Clemson’s second option at quarterback vs. Miami if necessary. “He's still not 100 percent on his left arm, so if he plays, he plays with a brace on it to protect it,” Swinney said. “But it's really more just the range of motion for him, kind of getting that back fully. But it's gotten a little better each day.” Swinney said Vizzina could play in an emergency. He wasn’t listed in the initial ACC availability report Sept. 30. The senior has 14 completions for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions this season. He was in the running for Clemson’s QB1 job with freshman Tait Reynolds during preseason camp, but Vizzina was ultimately named the starter in Week 1. Vizzina played three drives in the 22-7 win over Georgia Southern before Reynolds took over. The pair had previously split reps in a 51-10 loss to LSU. Reynolds was named the starter moving forward after the Georgia Southern game, but Swinney said the change had nothing to do with Vizzina’s health. In two career starts and four total games, Reynolds has thrown for 521 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Pearman, a fifth-year senior , joined Clemson as a walk-on in 2022. He has 10 passing attempts in his career, completing four for 43 yards. The D.W. Daniel graduate has played 33 career snaps. Reynolds will start for Clemson (3-1, 2-0 ACC) in its Oct. 3 matchup with No. 4 Miami (4-0, 2-0). Reach Jackson Castellano at jcastellano@po

As expected, sophomore tight end Luka Gilbert (undisclosed), redshirt junior running back CharMar “Marty” Brown (right knee), and sophomore wide receiver Joshua Moore (right shoulder) have been ruled out – the case for the rest of the season. Cornerbacks junior Romanas “OJ” Frederique Jr. (left shoulder) and Ja’Boree Antoine (undisclosed) are ruled out for the weekend. Newly added to the list, redshirt junior tight end Owen Ruskavich (undisclosed) has been ruled out. He’s logged a new collegiate career high, playing 26 snaps this season. He has shown promising signs this season. Marcelin Jr. is one of nine Hurricanes defenders with at least 10 tackles, including three solos and seven assists, a tackle for loss, and a forced pressure. Clemson has starting junior left guard Elyjah Thurmon (undisclosed) as questionable. home.blurb: Junior Xavier Lucas , who hasn't played since the season opener against Stanford , is listed as questionable for Saturday, according to the Atlantic Coast Conference's first availability report for the game released on Wednesday. Miami has been playing without three of its top cornerbacks basically all season, with starters Lucas and OJ Frederique out since the Stanford game and sophomore reserve Ja'Boree Antoine out since before the season began. Other players who sat out or were banged up against Central Michigan but don't appear on the availability report: running back Mark Fletcher Jr. , defensive linemen Ahmad Moten Sr. and Armondo Blount, and linebacker Kellen Wiley. Linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin is listed as questionable and reserve tight end Owen Ruskavich is out.
